topic: Contouring: contour interval and characteristics of contours, methods of contouring, interpolation, use of contour map
source: survey 350-455 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 371. An imaginary line connecting the points of equal elevation on the ground surface is known as
questions.explain: A contour line is a line drawn on a map connecting points of the same height above or below sea level.

questions.q: 372. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is known as
questions.explain: The vertical distance between two successive contour lines is the contour interval.

questions.q: 373. The minimum horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is known as
questions.explain: The horizontal distance between two consecutive contours is termed the horizontal equivalent.

questions.q: 374. Horizontal equivalent of uniform slope must be
questions.explain: For a uniform slope, the horizontal distance between contours (horizontal equivalent) remains constant or equal.

questions.q: 375. The contour interval depends upon
questions.explain: The choice of contour interval is influenced by ground terrain, map scale, and the specific needs of the project.

questions.q: 376. Contour interval is proportional
options: directly to the scale of map
inversely to the scale of map
directly to flatness of the ground
questions.explain: The interval is inversely proportional to the scale; smaller scales typically require larger intervals.

questions.q: 377. An imaginary line lying through the surface of ground, having a constant inclination to the horizontal is known as
questions.explain: A line maintaining a constant slope or inclination on the ground is called a contour gradient.

questions.q: 378. A series of closed contour lines on the map with higher to lower values inside them represents a
questions.explain: Closed contours with decreasing values toward the center indicate a depression or hollow.

questions.q: 379. The contour lines merge or cross one another on the map in case of
questions.explain: Contour lines only cross or merge in exceptional cases like caves or overhanging cliffs.

questions.q: 380. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a
questions.explain: Close spacing between contour lines indicates a rapid change in elevation, signifying a steep slope.

questions.q: 381. A series of straight, parallel and widely spaced contours on a map represents a
questions.explain: Straight, parallel, and equidistant contours represent a uniform inclined plane surface.

questions.q: 382. The contour lines are perpendicular to the
questions.explain: Contours cross both ridge and valley lines at right angles (90°).

questions.q: 383. The tacheometric method is more suitable method for preparing the contour map of a
questions.explain: Tacheometry is the most efficient method for contouring hilly or rough terrain.

questions.q: 384. The representation of general topography of a very flat terrain is possible only
options: by drawing contours at large interval
by giving spot levels at large interval
by giving spot levels to salient features of close interval
questions.explain: On flat ground, contours are far apart; spot levels at close intervals are used instead to show detail.

questions.q: 385. Contour represent at equal interval
questions.explain: When contours are spaced at equal horizontal intervals, they represent a uniform slope.

questions.q: 386. The contour close to each other represents
questions.explain: Contours drawn close together represent a steep incline/slope.

questions.q: 387. Contour interval, within the limits of a map
options: may vary according to the configuration
questions.explain: The contour interval must remain constant on a single map to avoid confusion in interpretation.

questions.q: 388. Two contour lines, having the same elevation
questions.explain: While generally they don't, in specific cases like an overhanging cliff, they can appear to cross.

questions.q: 389. Contour lines
questions.explain: Every contour line must eventually close upon itself, either within or outside the map limits.

questions.q: 390. Method of contour plotting can be done by
questions.explain: Various methods like squares, offsets, and cross-sections are used to locate points for contour plotting.

questions.q: 391. Contouring in hilly area is done by
questions.explain: The tacheometric method is ideal for hilly terrain because it allows the surveyor to find elevations and distances optically without the struggle of chaining over rough ground.

questions.q: 392. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of
questions.explain: In an overhanging cliff, the upper part of the land sticks out over the lower part, causing the contour lines to physically cross on a 2D map.

questions.q: 393. Pick up the odd statement
options: contour gives topography of the area
intervisibility between two points can be judged from a contour map
quantities of work can be computed from the contour map
for a vertical cliff contours seem to cross each other
questions.explain: Odd statement because contours for a vertical cliff 'unite' or 'merge' into one; they only 'cross' in an overhanging cliff.

questions.q: 394. Deep ravine means
options: very much difference in level within a little horizontal distance
questions.explain: A deep ravine is a narrow, steep-sided valley; on a map, it is shown by a very large change in elevation over a small horizontal distance, resulting in extremely close contour lines.

questions.q: 395. Height indicator is a
questions.explain: The Height Indicator is technically a scale or measuring device used to read vertical distances on specific surveying models or maps.

questions.q: 396. The direction of steepest slope on a contour, is
options: at an angles to the contour
at right angles to the contour
questions.explain: The steepest slope always occurs at right angles (90°) to the contour lines.

questions.q: 397. The direct method of contouring is
questions.explain: It is slow because you must physically walk the contour on the ground, but it is the most accurate because the points are actually located, so it's only practical for small plots.

questions.q: 398. In the direct method of contouring the process of locating points lying on a contour is known as
questions.explain: Vertical control is the process of establishing the elevation (Z) to find points on a specific contour line.

questions.q: 399. The spacing of cross-sections in indirect method of contouring depends upon
questions.explain: Rougher ground needs closer sections, large scale maps need more detail, and smaller intervals require more data points — all of these factors influence the spacing.

questions.q: 400. Find the contour interval for the map, 1: 25000 in IS & FPS
questions.explain: For a 1:25,000 scale map, the standard metric interval is 5m. Converting 5 meters to feet gives approximately 19.70ft.

questions.q: 401. Contours are used to determine
options: intervisibility of points on a contour map
area of the drainage basin and capacity of the reservoir
questions.explain: By drawing a profile between two points, checking intervisibility, calculating catchment basin sizes, and estimating earthwork volumes are all primary applications of contour maps.

questions.q: 402. Closed contours with higher value inside represents a
questions.explain: When contour values increase as you move toward the center, it represents a peak or a hill.

questions.q: 403. The order of accuracy of elevation of points obtained from a contour map is equal to
questions.explain: Standard mapping specifications state that 90% of tested elevations should be accurate within half of the contour interval.

questions.q: 404. The best method of interpolation of contours in direct method of contouring is by
questions.explain: Arithmetical computation is the most accurate method because it uses the exact ratio of the distance between two points and their difference in elevation.

questions.q: 405. In double line river, contours are
options: stopped at the bank of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
questions.explain: For a wide, 'double line' river, contour lines are stopped at the edge of the water surface.

questions.q: 406. The limit of water level in a river represents a
questions.explain: The surface of still water (or a slow-moving wide river) is always level, meaning every point on that surface is at the same elevation, forming a horizontal surface.

questions.q: 407. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from
questions.explain: A saddle is the lowest point on a ridge; starting from the saddle and working down the hill allows the highway to maintain a more consistent and gentle gradient.

questions.q: 408. For any point on the surface with a given inclination, contour gradient possible is
questions.explain: From any single point on a slope, you can turn in infinite directions to maintain a specific gradient, depending on how you curve your path.

questions.q: 409. For route survey of a contour map, method used is
questions.explain: Cross-profile (or cross-section) method involves taking sections perpendicular to the route's centerline, making it perfect for roads, canals, or railways.

questions.q: 410. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding the construction of
questions.explain: A dam requires knowing the exact topography of the entire valley to calculate flood zones, storage capacity, and spillway height, making a contour map absolutely essential.

questions.q: 411. The V-shaped contours shown below represent
questions.explain: When the V-shape points toward the higher elevation, it identifies the feature as a valley.
